evidence: User asked (2026-10-05, third play test) to replace the trial area with a wave spawn button. Each press spawns the next wave around the player on real Java terrain; after the last wave the last composition repeats with one extra enemy per type per repeat. EnemyType names verified against the local game's EnemyType enum (work/game-read/EnemyType.cs); prefabs come from the game's SpawnableObjectsDatabase.enemies at runtime and missing ones are skipped with a warning. A runtime navmesh follows the player so wave and Spawner Arm enemies can walk; climb of 1.1 blocks lets ground enemies step up one Java block. Fourth play test: the user expected the next wave after clearing one, so once J starts waves each cleared wave is followed by the next after a short delay; J still spawns the next one immediately. Fifth play test: no wave key. Every Minecraft night (day time 13000-23000, when vanilla monsters spawn) starts at wave 1 and advances after each clear; no new wave starts after dawn. Surface natural replacements are paused while night waves run so the two don't stack.
